newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES START WEEK MIXED.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES START WEEK MIXED.

text.p: HARARE, July 14 (Reutetr) - Short-term trading rates on Zimbabwe's liquid money market were quoted mixed at the start of the week on Monday, local money dealers said.
The market opened in surplus of Z$300 million with a further Z$500 million in maturities adding to liquidity.

The central Reserve Bank auctioned Z$500 million worth of 91-day treasury bills at a 24.96 percent discount. Another auction scheduled for later in the day was expected to raise Z$300 million through the sale of 58-day central bank paper.
Meanwhile, on the secondary market treasury bills were being sold at 24.85 percent, a notch up from 24.75, while call money edged up to 24 from 22.5 percent.

NCD bills redeemable after 30, 60 and 90 days were being bought softer at 26.5 percent from Friday's 27 percent but sold firmer at 26.25 percent from 25. Bank acceptance bills eased to 25.5 from 26 percent (buying) but were firmer at 25.25 percent compared to 24.85 (selling).
